title: Strange Signals, Ancient Glyphs, and Rogue DNA—The Latest from The Debrief
excerpt: Welcome to The Latest from The Debrief, where this week we're exploring signals from alien worlds, mysterious ancient writing systems, and more.
content:
Welcome to The Latest from The Debrief, where this week, we’re exploring discoveries that include signals from alien worlds, mysterious ancient writing systems, and innovations in the battle against cancer.

Ready for a look at what we’ve been tracking at The Debrief in recent days?

Let’s dive in. 

Strange Signals Were Just Detected Coming from an Alien World

Astronomers investigating unusual radio signals from a giant planet approximately 63 light-years from Earth believe they may have detected something never directly observed around an exoplanet before… and if confirmed, the discovery could give astronomers a new way to investigate the interiors of distant planets and eventually help assess whether other worlds possess magnetic environments capable of protecting their atmospheres—a potentially important factor in determining habitability.

Read the full story at The Debrief →

NASA’s New PRIMA Space Telescope Will Peer into the Unknown

NASA is moving forward with PRIMA, an ambitious new space telescope designed to explore the universe in far-infrared wavelengths that remain largely inaccessible to existing observatories. By examining this relatively underexplored portion of the electromagnetic spectrum, PRIMA could help astronomers investigate some of the coldest and most obscured regions of the cosmos, revealing phenomena hidden behind clouds of cosmic dust.

Read the full story at The Debrief →

Mysterious Glyphs Offer New Evidence of an Ancient Writing System

Three mysterious red symbols painted inside a shallow cave in Mexico may provide new evidence that the people of ancient Teotihuacan possessed a genuine writing system. Beyond revealing what may have occurred inside the cave centuries ago, the discovery adds new evidence to a longstanding archaeological debate over whether symbols associated with Teotihuacan represented a true system of writing rather than isolated decorative or emblematic imagery.

Read the full story at The Debrief →

Unusual “Rogue DNA” That Feeds Cancer May Have an Achilles’ Heel

Some of the most aggressive cancers exploit an unusual form of genetic material called extrachromosomal DNA, or ecDNA, which exists outside the chromosomes and can help tumors rapidly evolve, resist treatment and amplify cancer-promoting genes. Now, researchers have identified what may be a critical vulnerability, offering a promising new target in the effort to exploit one of cancer’s unusual genetic adaptations against itself.

Read the full story at The Debrief →

And There’s More…

Scientists Studied Decades of Magic Tricks—and Revealed Something Strange About How the Brain Sees Reality

Magic works by exploiting assumptions our brains make about the world around us. By examining decades of research into illusions and sleight of hand, scientists are uncovering new clues about attention, perception, and how the brain constructs our experience of reality.

Read the full story →

Physicists Have Made a Microscopic Discovery That May Hold the Key to Building Better Quantum Computers

A discovery at the microscopic scale could help researchers overcome some of the persistent challenges involved in developing practical quantum computers, offering fresh insight into how scientists might build more stable and reliable quantum technologies.
